paragraphs.text: Nvidia's board is preparing to remove Jensen Huang as chief executive, according to a Wall Street Journal report published on November 11, 2026, that cited people familiar with the matter. Reuters and Fortune both relayed the report, which said the board could meet as soon as that Wednesday to decide his future.
Huang co-founded Nvidia in 1993 and has run it for 33 years, according to Fortune. Fortune described Nvidia as a $4 trillion chipmaking company, and a removal would end Huang's reign over it.
Two affairs at the center of the report

According to Reuters, the Journal said the board was moving against Huang after he had two extramarital affairs, including one with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy. The report came days after Huang acknowledged on Sunday, November 8, that he had been unfaithful to his wife.

The controversy involves a woman named Alice Huang, whom US intelligence says facilitated shipments of Nvidia chips to Chinese firms, Reuters reported. The case has drawn scrutiny from lawmakers, investors and the company's own board.

Separately, The New York Times reported earlier on November 11 that Huang had a relationship with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia's vice president of health care, who reported to him. Reuters said the Times cited five people who had worked at the company. Fortune said Powell could not be reached for comment and that, according to her LinkedIn profile, she has been at Nvidia for nearly two decades.

Nvidia's board had already opened an investigation into whether Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence operation. In a statement quoted by Fortune, the board said it had "no reason to believe that either national security or NVIDIA secrets were compromised" and that its inquiry would examine "all available information."
Nvidia did not immediately respond to requests for comment on the latest report, and Reuters said it could not immediately verify it.

Nvidia shares fell about 8% in after-hours trading following the report, Reuters said, while Fortune put the decline at more than 9%. Reuters added that the company has lost more than $300 billion in market value since news of the affair with Alice Huang first broke.

The pressure lands while the business is still growing quickly. Fortune noted that Nvidia reported $215.9 billion in revenue for fiscal 2026, up 65% from the year before, and guided to about $108 billion in revenue for the third quarter of fiscal 2027. Chief financial officer Colette Kress has said the company expects 70% revenue growth in fiscal 2028.
A company built around one leader

Fortune reported that Huang has about 60 direct reports and sits at the center of most major decisions. The board operates without a chair, and the company has no clear succession plan, the magazine said. D.A. Davidson analyst Gil Luria told Fortune that the circumstances "hasten a transition the company is not prepared for."

Reuters noted that Nvidia's chips are used to train AI models and run services such as OpenAI's ChatGPT, and that Huang's exit would create a leadership vacuum at a company central to the race between the United States and China in artificial intelligence.

For NeuraFeed, the larger question is less about Nvidia's products than about authority. Nvidia's revenue keeps growing, but customers, partners and governments have long dealt with Huang personally. Any successor would have to hold those relationships together while the board's investigation and congressional scrutiny continue.
The key signal to watch is a formal statement from Nvidia's board on Huang's role and on who, if anyone, would lead the company in the interim.
